text:
anna: Heads-up — hitting a slow memory creep in KV cache on long-context tests (8k tokens). After ~6h one worker shows ~37% fragmentation and steady RSS growth (~120MB/hr). No obvious leak in application code, looks allocator-related.

tom: Oof. Which allocator config are you running? any pattern in block sizes?

anna: default allocator (microblock=192, slot=32, page=64KB). The tail is mostly tiny free slots but large contiguous free runs are rare. Dump attached below.

perf-bot: perf-snapshot @3841123500
```
kv_stats:
  total_alloc: 12GB
  total_free: 4.4GB
  fragmentation_est: 0.37
  bucket_histogram: {32: 1.1GB, 64: 600MB, 192: 2.2GB, 1024+: 0.5GB}
  avg_free_run_len: 2.3
  long_context_rss_delta_6h: +720MB
```

sasha: Those numbers scream microblock mismatch. Large portion in 192B bucket — likely many short-lived keys with varying TTLs causing interleaving. Buddy/coalescing not triggering because free-run < 4 pages.

kevin: FYI I tried a naive compaction background worker in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1234 — it reduces fragmentation to ~18% but introduced CPU spikes during compaction at mid qps (~50-70 qps) because compaction scans are synchronous per-page.

anna: saw that PR, thanks. The CPU spike is the blocker. We need a low-latency compaction strategy (incremental + throttled) or smarter allocation to avoid creating those small holes.

tom: Can we try two experiments: 1) increase microblock to 256 to reduce internal fragmentation, 2) enable async incremental compaction that only coalesces when free_run_len >= 4 and max_work_ms_per_tick=5ms. Quick A/B in the perf harness?

sasha: Sounds good. Small note: increasing microblock reduces memory pressure but may increase wasted space for truly tiny values. For our 8k long-context workload, majority of KV entries are ~140-220B so 256 may be better.

kevin: I can wire async compaction + pacing. Pseudocode for compaction tick:
```
function compaction_tick(max_ms) {
  start = now()
  while(now() - start < max_ms) {
    page = next_candidate_page()
    if(!page) break
    if(page.free_run_len >= 4) coalesce(page)
    else continue
  }
}
```
Set max_ms=5 for canary.

anna: Great. Also add telemetry: kv_frag_percent_by_bucket and kv_compaction_cpu_ms_per_min. We need to correlate compaction cpu with latency tail.

perf-bot: scheduled experiment run: branch=kv/async-compaction-3841, microblock=256, max_ms=5, run=long-context-8k-6h. Started @3841124000.

perf-bot: experiment summary @3841125800
```
before:
  frag: 0.37, rss_growth_6h: +720MB, p99_lat: 38ms
after:
  frag: 0.11, rss_growth_6h: +120MB, p99_lat: 41ms (with two 6-8ms compaction ticks), cpu_budget_used: 0.9%
```

anna: That's promising — fragmentation down a lot, rss growth almost gone. p99 up by ~3ms but within SLO. Need to validate at higher QPS.

tom: Next steps: 1) run canary at 200 qps and watch compaction CPU and tail; 2) tweak microblock to 224 as middle ground; 3) add bucket-aware batching so allocator tries to place same-size entries together where possible.

kevin: I'll open a smaller PR that includes: async compaction tick + telemetry + config knobs (microblock_size, compaction_max_ms, free_run_threshold). Link incoming.

sasha: TL;DR: adaptive approach worked — fewer compaction cycles, coalescing threshold prevented work on tiny runs, and microblock bump reduced internal waste. Nice win. :thumbsup:

anna: Thanks all. I'll schedule the 200qps canary for tomorrow morning and add an alert if kv_frag_percent > 0.2 or rss_growth_1h > 50MB.

kevin: PR posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1240 — please review.

tom: Reviewing now. Quick request — add a short synthetic test that forces interleaved short-lived keys so we don't regress.

anna: Will add that test and share results once canary completes.
